def literal_whole_word_regex(pattern):
    """
    Literal, case-insensitive pattern match.
    If the pattern begins/ends with an alphanumeric character, require
    non-alphanumeric boundaries so 'too' will not match inside 'took'.
    Internal spaces in list entries are allowed to match one or more spaces.

    prefix = r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])" if pattern[0].isalnum() else ""

from pathlib import Path
import re
from copy import copy

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.cell.rich_text import CellRichText, TextBlock
from openpyxl.cell.text import InlineFont

input_path = Path("/mnt/data/spreadsheet/73-45/1_73-45_input.xlsx")
output_path = Path("/mnt/data/outputs/73-45_1_458e5469/1_73-45_output.xlsx")
output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

wb = load_workbook(input_path, rich_text=True)
ws = wb["Sheet1"]

TARGET_COL = "BD"
START_ROW = 2
END_ROW = 308
SAMPLE_END_ROW = 33  # 32 manually formatted sample rows: BD2:BD33

RED_RGB = "FFFF0000"


def font_is_bold_red(font):
    if font is None:
        return False

    bold = getattr(font, "b", None)
    if bold is None:
        bold = getattr(font, "bold", False)

    if not bold:
        return False

    color = getattr(font, "color", None)
    if color is None:
        return False

    rgb = getattr(color, "rgb", None)
    if rgb:
        return str(rgb).upper().endswith("FF0000")

    indexed = getattr(color, "indexed", None)
    # Excel's standard red is often indexed color 10
    if indexed == 10:
        return True

    return False


def iter_rich_runs(cell):
    """Yield (text, font) pairs from a cell, including rich-text runs."""
    value = cell.value

    if value is None:
        return

    if isinstance(value, CellRichText):
        for part in value:
            if isinstance(part, TextBlock):
                yield str(part.text), part.font
            else:
                yield str(part), None
    else:
        yield str(value), cell.font


# Extract the manually highlighted bold-red patterns from the 32 sample rows.
patterns = []
seen = set()

for row in range(START_ROW, min(SAMPLE_END_ROW, END_ROW) + 1):
    cell = ws[f"{TARGET_COL}{row}"]

    for text, font in iter_rich_runs(cell):
        if font_is_bold_red(font):
            pattern = text.strip(" \t\r\n,;:")
            if pattern:
                key = «redacted»                if key not in seen:
                    seen.add(key)
                    patterns.append(pattern)

# Prefer longer patterns first so phrases are considered before shorter words.
patterns.sort(key=«redacted» reverse=True)


def whole_word_literal_regex(pattern):
    """
    Build a case-insensitive literal-search regex that treats alphanumeric
    characters as word characters.  This allows matching 'too' as a whole word
    without matching it inside 'took'.
    """
    escaped = re.escape(pattern)
    escaped = re.sub(r"\\\s+", r"\\s+", escaped)

    prefix = r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])" if pattern and pattern[0].isalnum() else ""
    suffix = r"(?![A-Za-z0-9])" if pattern and pattern[-1].isalnum() else ""

    return re.compile(prefix + escaped + suffix, re.IGNORECASE)


compiled_patterns = [whole_word_literal_regex(p) for p in patterns]


def merge_intervals(intervals):
    if not intervals:
        return []

    intervals = sorted(intervals)
    merged = [list(intervals[0])]

    for start, end in intervals[1:]:
        if start <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], end)
        else:
            merged.append([start, end])

    return [(s, e) for s, e in merged]


highlight_font = InlineFont(b=True, color=RED_RGB)

# Apply the extracted search patterns to BD2:BD308 only.
for row in range(START_ROW, END_ROW + 1):
    cell = ws[f"{TARGET_COL}{row}"]
    value = cell.value

    if value is None or str(value) == "":
        continue

    # Convert any existing rich text to plain text, then rebuild formatting.
    text = "".join(run_text for run_text, _ in iter_rich_runs(cell))

    intervals = []
    for regex in compiled_patterns:
        for match in regex.finditer(text):
            intervals.append((match.start(), match.end()))

    intervals = merge_intervals(intervals)

    if not intervals:
        # Keep the cell text as plain text if no searched pattern is present.
        cell.value = text
        continue

    rich_value = CellRichText()
    pos = 0

    for start, end in intervals:
        if start > pos:
            rich_value.append(text[pos:start])
        rich_value.append(TextBlock(copy(highlight_font), text[start:end]))
        pos = end

    if pos < len(text):
        rich_value.append(text[pos:])

    cell.value = rich_value

wb.save(output_path)
